findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running Forge's release consistency test or syncing its checkout.
The checked-in classifier still has the old folder-matching rule and an outdated `test_readers` implementation. Sync embeds the current `src/forge/docskip.py` into this file, as shown at `src/forge/prcheck.py:431`. Consequently, `tests/test_release_version.py:48` reports `.forge/review-tests.py` as stale and fails. Regenerate it using the current checkout.
findings.title: Regenerate the checked-in CI classifier from the changed source

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - separate tests read different files in the same directory.
The AST walker also visits intermediate expressions, so a test that reads `docs/unrelated.md` now matches a change to `docs/guide.md` through its intermediate `... / 'docs'` expression. This selects the deliberately failing unrelated test in `tests/test_file_relative_docs_run_tests.py:53`; the existing `forge test --change` assertion at line 80 then fails. It also expands client test runs for unrelated files.
findings.title: Do not treat every file path's intermediate directory as a folder read

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: rare - a board asset is edited in a subdirectory, or a Python file is added directly under `board_app`.
The full Done-when item is: A pull request that changes a file under src/forge/board_app runs the board's browser tests in its check, in Forge's own repo; and the change says what a new and an existing client repo each get.
The new match only recognizes files whose immediate parent is the referenced folder. For example, a change to `src/forge/board_app/item-controls/view.js` does not match the `board_app` reference in `tests/test_board_server.py:338`. Separately, `src/forge/fasttest.py:449` excludes Python files from this folder-reader rule. Neither case selects the board browser tests solely because the file is under `board_app`, as the item requires.
findings.title: Not done: A pull request that changes a file under src/forge/board_app runs the board's browser tests in its check

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a pull request changes a board script or stylesheet.
The named proof replaces the repo's test command with `--collect-only`, invokes `forge test --pytest` directly, and checks only the printed names of two test files. It does not establish that the pull request's `forge test --change` check executes the browser tests. It would still pass if the check excluded platform tests or if other board browser files, such as `tests/test_board_shell.py`, stopped being selected.
findings.title: Gate: prove the pull request check runs the board browser tests

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - initializing a client repo or upgrading one adopted on an earlier release.
The named proof uses a bare temporary Git repo and writes a new `forge.toml` itself; it never initializes a client or upgrades an earlier-adopted client. The new and adopted cases in `tests/test_board_server.py` exercise asset serving, not picker selection. The promised picker behavior and lack of a required settings change therefore have no test at either client boundary.
findings.title: Gate: cover the folder picker in new and earlier-adopted client repos

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running the suite on Windows from a checkout whose virtual-environment path contains spaces.
`shlex.join` surrounds that executable path with POSIX single quotes. The picker runs the configured command through the Windows shell (`src/forge/fasttest.py:825`), where those quotes do not protect spaces, so both new platform tests fail before pytest starts.
findings.title: Quote the test executable for Windows paths containing spaces

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round with a narrow rule: only a test that lists a folder's files itself is related to the files in that folder

why: The pull-request check picks tests by the Python files that changed, so a change to the board's script or style files (src/forge/board_app) merges with the board's browser tests not run; the tab-in-address fix made the default branch red this way
